en: to take part in; to side with

examples.ko: 그 사람은 범죄에 가담한 적이 없어요.
examples.en: That person has never been involved in any crime.
My friends joined the fight, and things got worse.
Is there anyone who will join this plan?
There is a rumor going around that someone took part in the fraud case.

examples.ko: 저는 그 일에 가담하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to get involved in that.
Nobody joined, so the plan fell through.

explain: '참가하다'는 대회나 모임처럼 평범한 자리에 쓰지만, '가담하다'는 주로 나쁜 일이나 한쪽 편에 힘을 보탤 때 써요. 좋은 행사에 '가담하다'를 쓰면 어색해요.

phrases.example: 그는 범행에 가담한 혐의로 조사를 받았어요.
phrases.en: He was questioned on suspicion of taking part in the crime.
phrases.nuance_ko: '범행', '시위' 같은 말과 함께 쓰면 나쁜 일에 힘을 보탠다는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With words like 범행 (crime), it clearly means helping out in a bad act.

phrases.en: All the participants were punished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일에 참여한 사람을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for a person who took part in something bad.

phrases.en: In the end, he sided with the opposing party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸움이나 다툼에서 한쪽 편에 서서 돕는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to take one side and help it in a fight or dispute.

explain_en: Usually negative — joining something bad like a prank or crime. 참가하다 is for ordinary events and contests, but 가담하다 is mostly used when someone joins in something bad or takes one side. Using it for a nice event sounds odd.

dis.h: get involved, usually in something bad
gh: join others in a cause or event

p.n: 범죄에 참여했어요 sounds odd. 가담하다 carries a negative nuance, while 참여하다 is neutral.

examples.ko: 농부가 봄이 오기 전에 밭을 갈아엎었어요.
examples.en: The farmer plowed the field before spring came.

examples.ko: 이 땅을 갈아엎고 옥수수를 심을 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to plow this land and plant corn.
I can hear the sound of a tractor plowing the rice field.

examples.ko: 계획이 마음에 안 들어서 처음부터 갈아엎기로 했어요.
examples.en: I didn't like the plan, so I decided to scrap it and start over.
The freshly plowed field smelled of earth.
My team leader told us to overhaul the proposal completely.

explain: 기본 뜻은 쟁기나 트랙터로 땅을 뒤집는 거예요. 그래서 계획이나 방식을 처음부터 완전히 새로 하자고 할 때 '싹 갈아엎다'처럼 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: I plowed the field over and sowed the seeds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅을 뒤집은 다음 다른 일을 이어서 할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for turning the soil and then doing the next step.

phrases.example: 계획을 싹 갈아엎고 처음부터 다시 하기로 했어요.
phrases.en: We decided to scrap the plan and start over.
phrases.nuance_ko: '싹'을 붙여 계획이나 방식을 완전히 새로 한다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '싹' it is a figure of speech for redoing a plan or method completely.

phrases.en: The ground is hard, so we have to plow it over first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해야 할 일을 말하는 활용으로, 농사 이야기에서 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form for saying something must be done, often heard in farming talk.

explain_en: Its basic meaning is turning over soil with a plow or tractor. Because of that, people also use it figuratively, as in '싹 갈아엎다', to mean completely redoing a plan or method from scratch.

examples.en: The subway on my commute these days is real torture.

examples.ko: 여름에 에어컨 없이 지내는 건 고역이었어요.
examples.en: Getting through summer without air conditioning was an ordeal.

examples.ko: 매일 두 시간씩 걷는 일이 저에게는 고역이에요.
examples.en: Walking two hours every day is a real chore for me.

examples.ko: 무거운 짐을 들고 계단을 오르는 고역을 겪었어요.
examples.en: I went through the ordeal of climbing stairs with heavy bags.

examples.ko: 이 일이 고역처럼 느껴질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: There are times when this work feels like drudgery.

examples.ko: 긴 회의를 가만히 듣고 있는 것도 고역이에요.
examples.en: Sitting through a long meeting is also a torment.

explain: '힘들다'보다 하기 싫고 괴로운 일이라는 느낌이 강해요. '고역이다', '고역을 치르다', '고역을 겪다'처럼 쓰고, 사람이 아니라 '일'이나 '상황'이 주어가 돼요.

phrases.example: 무거운 짐을 들고 계단을 오르는 건 고역이에요.
phrases.en: Climbing the stairs with heavy bags is a real ordeal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하기 싫고 괴로운 일을 말할 때 가장 기본으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic way to describe a painful, unwanted task.

phrases.en: I went through an ordeal moving yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들고 괴로운 일을 억지로 해냈다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests having pushed through a hard, unpleasant task.

phrases.en: I finally got free from the ordeal of the long commute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 괴롭던 일이 끝나서 편해졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a painful task is over and you feel relieved.

explain_en: It feels stronger than '힘들다', suggesting something unpleasant and painful to go through. It appears in '고역이다', '고역을 치르다', and '고역을 겪다', and the subject is a task or situation, not a person.

examples.en: The pilgrims prayed as they walked the path of penance.
This hike was practically an ordeal.

examples.ko: 매일 새벽에 일어나는 게 저에게는 고행이에요.
examples.en: Getting up at dawn every day is torture for me.
I heard the monk practiced asceticism in the mountains.
The subway on my commute feels like an ordeal.
A marathon is closer to an ordeal than to fun.

explain: 원래는 종교에서 몸을 괴롭히며 하는 수행을 뜻하지만, 일상에서는 정말 힘든 일을 조금 과장해서 '고행 같다'고 말해요. '고생'보다 스스로 견뎌 내야 하는 힘든 일이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: The monk practiced asceticism in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종교에서 몸을 괴롭히는 수행을 한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in the religious sense of practicing self-denial.

phrases.example: 매일 만원 지하철을 타는 건 고행 같아요.
phrases.en: Riding the packed subway every day feels like a penance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 일을 조금 과장해서 말할 때 쓰는 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday expression for exaggerating how hard something is.

phrases.en: The pilgrimage, walking from dawn, was a path of hardship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들게 견뎌야 하는 길이나 과정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a path or process that must be endured with difficulty.

explain_en: Originally it means religious training that puts the body through pain, but in daily life people exaggerate and say something is '고행 같다' when it is really tough. Compared with '고생', it feels more like an ordeal you have to endure yourself.

en: to come to a standstill; to become bogged down; to be deadlocked

examples.ko: 협상이 몇 달째 교착해서 아무 결론이 안 나요.
examples.en: The negotiations have been deadlocked for months, so there's no conclusion.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 대화가 교착하면 경제에도 영향이 있어요.
examples.en: If talks between the two countries stall, the economy is affected too.

examples.ko: 교착한 상황을 풀려고 새 제안을 내놓았어요.
examples.en: They made a new proposal to break the deadlock.

examples.ko: 회의가 교착해도 포기하지 말고 계속 이야기해 봐요.
examples.en: Even if the meeting gets stuck, let's not give up and keep talking.
I saw on the news that the labor-management talks hit a deadlock.
The matter that had been stuck finally got resolved.

explain: 보통은 '교착 상태에 빠지다'라고 많이 말해요. 협상, 대화, 경제 같은 큰 일에 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '막혀 있어요', '꼼짝도 못 해요'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 두 회사의 협상이 교착 상태에 빠졌어요.
phrases.en: The negotiations between the two companies have fallen into a deadlock.
phrases.nuance_ko: '교착하다'보다 훨씬 자주 쓰는 형태로, 일이 더 나아가지 못할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used far more often than 교착하다 itself, for when things can't move forward.

phrases.example: 양쪽이 만나서 교착 상태를 풀기로 했어요.
phrases.en: Both sides decided to meet and break the deadlock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막힌 상황을 해결하려고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when trying to resolve a stalemate.

phrases.example: 회의에서 의견이 갈려서 계속 막혀 있어요.
phrases.en: Opinions split in the meeting, so we're still stuck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 교착한 상황을 쉽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday way to describe a stalled situation.

explain_en: People usually say '교착 상태에 빠지다' (fall into a deadlock). It is used for big matters like negotiations, talks or the economy, while in everyday talk people say '막혀 있어요' or '꼼짝도 못 해요'.

en: to rescue; to save; to deliver

examples.en: The hero saved the villagers.

examples.ko: 위험에 빠진 아이들을 구원한 소방관이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a firefighter who rescued children in danger.
I felt that music saved me.
Who will save this country?

examples.ko: 위기에 빠진 회사를 구원하고 싶어서 직접 나섰어요.
examples.en: I stepped in myself because I wanted to save the company from the crisis.

examples.ko: 종교가 사람을 구원한다고 믿는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people believe religion saves people.

explain: 일상에서는 '구하다', '도와주다'를 쓰고, 구원하다는 큰 위기나 종교에서 사람을 건진다는 무거운 느낌이에요. 영화나 소설에서 '세상을 구원하다'처럼 나와요. 작은 도움에는 어울리지 않아요.

phrases.en: The firefighter saved the child.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구원하다'보다 쉽고 일상적이라서 작은 위기에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more everyday than 구원하다, and usable for smaller crises too.

phrases.en: The hero in the movie saves the world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 소설에서 자주 나오는, 무거운 느낌의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A heavy-toned pairing often seen in movies and novels.

phrases.en: The village was saved thanks to that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구원을 받는 쪽에서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression from the side of the one being saved.

explain_en: Save spiritually or emotionally, deliverance (절망에서 구원하다) In daily life Koreans say '구하다' or '도와주다'; 구원하다 carries a heavy sense of rescuing someone from a great crisis or in a religious sense. It appears in films and novels, as in '세상을 구원하다'. It does not suit small favors.

dis.h: save from suffering or sin, deliverance
gh: rescue someone from danger or disaster
get someone out of captivity or a trap

p.n: 구조하다 would sound like a physical rescue, not spiritual salvation.

t90.ax: I felt that music saved me.

examples.en: I was suddenly asked a question and got cornered.
Thanks to my friend, I got out of a tight spot.

examples.ko: 상대 팀을 궁지로 몰아넣는 작전이 통했어요.
examples.en: The tactic of driving the opposing team into a corner worked.

examples.ko: 궁지에 몰린 상대는 오히려 더 세게 덤벼요.
examples.en: A cornered opponent comes at you even harder.
He escaped the predicament with a single remark.

examples.ko: 이번 일로 회사가 큰 궁지에 처했어요.
examples.en: Because of this matter, the company is in a serious predicament.

explain: 보통 '궁지에 몰리다/빠지다/처하다'처럼 '에'와 함께 써요. '곤경'과 비슷하지만, 궁지는 도망갈 곳 없이 몰린 느낌이 더 강해요. 벗어날 때는 '궁지에서 벗어나다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 궁지에 몰린 쥐가 고양이를 문다더니, 약한 팀이 끝까지 달려들었어요.
phrases.en: They say a cornered rat bites the cat, and the weaker team kept fighting to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 절박한 상황에 몰리면 약한 사람도 강한 상대에게 필사적으로 덤빈다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb saying that even the weak will fight desperately against a stronger opponent when driven into a corner.
phrases.en_equiv: a cornered rat will fight back

explain_en: Cornered by trouble or pressure — everyday (궁지에 몰리다) It usually goes with '에', as in '궁지에 몰리다/빠지다/처하다'. It is similar to '곤경' (hardship), but '궁지' conveys more strongly the feeling of being backed into a corner with no way out. To get out you say '궁지에서 벗어나다'.

en: to stay; to settle; to stay put

examples.en: I meant to rest for a moment but just ended up staying put.

examples.ko: 친구 집에서 며칠 묵으려다 한 달이나 눌러앉았어요.
examples.en: I meant to stay at my friend's place a few days but ended up staying a whole month.
That player decided to stay with the team.
Is it okay if I just stay here?

examples.ko: 서울에 잠시 온 건데 십 년째 눌러앉아 살고 있어요.
examples.en: I only came to Seoul for a while, but I've ended up living here for ten years.
What do we do if the guest doesn't leave and just stays?

explain: 가려던 곳으로 안 가고 그 자리에 계속 머물게 될 때 써요. '머무르다'가 중립적인 말이라면, 이 말은 '어쩌다 오래 있게 됐다'는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The cafe was so comfortable that I just stayed put.
phrases.nuance_ko: '버리다'를 붙이면 어쩌다 계속 머물렀다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 버리다 strengthens the sense of ending up staying.

phrases.example: 여행하다가 이 도시가 좋아서 눌러앉고 말았어요.
phrases.en: While traveling, I liked this city so much that I ended up settling here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획과 달리 그곳에 자리 잡게 됐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you settled there, unlike your original plan.

phrases.example: 친구 집에서 하루 종일 눌러앉아 있었어요.
phrases.en: I stayed at my friend's place all day long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한곳에 오래 머무는 모습을 시간 표현과 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes staying in one place for long, with a time phrase.

explain_en: Stay on instead of leaving, spoken (동네에 눌러앉다) It is used when you don't go where you meant to and keep staying put. While '머무르다' is neutral, this word carries a feeling of ending up staying longer than planned.

t90.ax: Is it okay if I just stay here?

en: staying shut in at home; seclusion

examples.en: As the seclusion dragged on, fans grew worried.

examples.ko: 작가는 두문불출 끝에 새 소설을 완성했어요.
examples.en: After a long seclusion, the author finished a new novel.

examples.ko: 두문불출 중인 친구에게 안부 메시지를 보냈어요.
examples.en: I sent a check-in message to my friend who is staying shut in.
He stayed shut in all vacation, so Mom is worried.
As his reclusion went on, rumors spread.

examples.ko: 두문불출 생활을 끝내고 오랜만에 밖으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: I ended my life of staying shut in and went outside for the first time in a long while.

explain: 집에 틀어박혀 밖에 나가지 않는 것을 뜻하는 네 글자 표현이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 유명인이나 작가가 모습을 보이지 않을 때 자주 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '집에 틀어박혀 있다'고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: That singer has been staying out of sight lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 집에만 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone who is currently staying at home.
phrases.en_equiv: to be shut away at home

phrases.example: 그는 오랜 두문불출을 깨고 공개 행사에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: He broke his long seclusion and appeared at a public event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오랫동안 집에 있다가 밖으로 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone comes out after a long time at home.

phrases.en: I stayed shut in at home all weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 이 표현을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is more common in everyday conversation.
phrases.en_equiv: to shut oneself in at home

explain_en: This four-character expression means shutting yourself in and not going out. It often appears in news and writing when a celebrity or author is out of sight, while in everyday talk people say '집에 틀어박혀 있다'.

examples.en: As soon as we opened the door, customers rushed in all at once.
When a typhoon comes, waves surge onto the shore.
People flooded in at lunchtime, and it was hectic.

examples.ko: 연말에는 일이 한꺼번에 밀어닥치는 때가 많아요.
examples.en: At the end of the year, work often piles up all at once.
I'm worried that reporters will suddenly swarm in.

examples.ko: 세일 첫날 사람들이 밀어닥치면서 가게가 난리였어요.
examples.en: On the first day of the sale, people poured in and the store was chaos.

explain: 사람, 물, 일이 큰 힘으로 한꺼번에 몰려올 때 써요. '몰려오다'보다 기세가 센 느낌이에요. '일이 밀어닥치다'처럼 일이나 변화가 갑자기 많아질 때도 써요.

phrases.en: Customers come in all at once at lunchtime.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 비슷하지만 기세가 덜 세고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The meaning is similar but less forceful, and it is more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: Orders pour in all at once at the end of the year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 일이 계속 많이 들어올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when people or work keep coming in great numbers.

phrases.en: When I came back from vacation, work piled up all at once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 할 일이 갑자기 많아져서 감당하기 힘들 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a phrase for when work suddenly becomes too much to handle.

explain_en: Crowds, waves, or hardships pressing in suddenly in large numbers. It is used when people, water or work come all at once with great force. It feels stronger than '몰려오다'. It is also used for a sudden flood of work or change, as in '일이 밀어닥치다'.

examples.en: The baby is crying and kicking his legs about.

examples.ko: 바둥바둥 아끼며 살아도 돈이 잘 안 모여요.
examples.en: Even though I struggle to save, money doesn't build up.
The fly caught in the spider web is struggling and squirming.
He worked desperately to pay off his debt.

examples.ko: 바둥바둥 애를 써도 일이 풀리지 않아요.
examples.en: No matter how hard I strain, things don't work out.
The child is wriggling around to be picked up.

explain: 팔다리를 작게 흔들며 애쓰는 모습을 말해요. 아기나 작은 동물 이야기뿐 아니라 '바둥바둥 살다'처럼 힘들게 노력하는 모습에도 써요. 약간 안쓰러운 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: I'm struggling hard to pay off my debt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 상황에서 벗어나려고 힘들게 노력하는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes working hard and with difficulty to escape a tough situation.

phrases.en: I'm scraping by day after day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넉넉하지 않게 힘들게 사는 삶을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes living a hard life without much to spare.

phrases.example: 아기가 버둥버둥 움직이며 잠을 안 자요.
phrases.en: The baby is wriggling around and won't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바둥바둥'과 비슷하지만 조금 더 크게 움직이는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 바둥바둥 but with bigger movements.

explain_en: Repeated flailing of limbs, or desperate effort. It shows small arms and legs moving as one tries hard. It is used for babies and small animals, and also for people working hard against difficulty, as in '바둥바둥 살다'. It carries a slightly pitiful feeling.

t90.ax: He worked desperately to pay off his debt.

examples.en: The child snapped a branch just for fun.
You must not snap the chopsticks.
I got angry and snapped the pencil.
We snapped off branches and made a fire.
We broke the cookie in half and shared it.
Please don't snap that stick.

explain: '부러뜨리다'와 비슷한데 손으로 힘을 줘서 뚝 꺾는 느낌이 더 강해요. 가늘고 긴 것에 주로 써요. '르' 불규칙이라서 '분질러요', '분질렀어요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: The wind broke the tree branch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 일반적인 말이고, 손으로 힘을 준 느낌이 꼭 있지는 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: More general, and doesn't always imply force applied by hand.

phrases.en: I get angry and snap my pencil.
phrases.nuance_ko: '르' 불규칙 활용이라 '분지르다'가 '분질러요'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A 르-irregular verb, so 분지르다 becomes 분질러요.

phrases.en: Please don't snap off the flower branches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 부탁에서 하지 말라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in signs or requests to tell someone not to do it.

explain_en: It is close to '부러뜨리다' but feels more like snapping something off sharply with your hands, usually something thin and long. It is a '르' irregular verb, so it becomes '분질러요' and '분질렀어요'.

examples.en: I got sick from exhaustion of my energy.
The project stopped because the budget ran out.
Burnout is called exhaustion of the mind.
The discount lasts only until stock runs out.
I was so worn out that I took a day off.

examples.ko: 자원 소진을 막기 위해 아껴 써야 해요.
examples.en: We have to use things sparingly to prevent depletion of resources.

explain: 소진은 가진 힘, 돈, 물건이 다 써서 바닥나는 것을 말해요. 안내문에서는 '재고 소진 시까지', '예산 소진'처럼 쓰고, 사람의 상태를 말할 때는 '번아웃'과 비슷한 '탈진' 느낌이에요. 말로 할 때는 '다 떨어지다', '바닥나다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The discount lasts until the stock runs out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게 안내문에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in store notices.

phrases.en: I'm resting today because my energy is drained.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 다 빠진 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state where energy is completely used up.

phrases.en: The rice has run out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 소진 대신 쓰는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy spoken alternative to 소진.

explain_en: Being used up completely, of energy or resources (체력 소진) Sojin means running out of strength, money, or goods until nothing is left. Notices use it in phrases like 재고 소진 시까지 and 예산 소진, and for people it is close to burnout or 탈진. In speech, 다 떨어지다 and 바닥나다 are far more natural.

en: to be brought under control; to be recovered

examples.en: I'm glad the accident was dealt with quickly.
It takes time until the confusion is sorted out.
Only after the fight was settled did everyone smile.
The problem wasn't resolved, so the meeting dragged on.
I'll contact you as soon as things are under control.
It was a big mistake, but it was handled well.

explain: 수습되다는 어지럽거나 문제가 된 일이 정리되어 가라앉을 때 써요. 사고, 소동, 논란처럼 일이 터진 뒤의 말과 잘 어울려요. 소리가 같은 '수습 사원'의 수습은 다른 말이니 따로 외우세요.

phrases.en: The problem has not been sorted out yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 아직 가라앉지 않았을 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for when things have not settled yet.

phrases.en: The chaotic situation was finally brought under control.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사태', '사고'처럼 문제가 터진 일과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs well with troubles like '사태' or '사고'.

phrases.en: The CEO handled the accident himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 일을 정리하는 쪽은 능동형 '수습하다'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, for a person sorting things out.

explain_en: 수습되다 is used when a messy or troublesome situation gets sorted out and calms down. It pairs with accidents, commotions and controversies, that is, things after trouble has broken out. The 수습 in 수습 사원 (trainee) sounds the same but is a different word.
